COW2019:s17.heading: Time limit for payment of wages
COW2019:s17.text:
17. Time limit for payment of wages.—(1) The employer shall pay or cause to be paid wages to the 
employees, engaged on— 
(i) daily basis, at the end of the shift; 
(ii) weekly basis, on the last working day of the week, that is to say, before the weekly holiday; 
(iii) fortnightly basis, before the end of the second day after the end of the fortnight; 
(iv) monthly basis, before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month. 
(2) Where an employee has been— 
(i) removed or dismissed from service; or 
(ii) retrenched or has resigned from service, or became unemployed due to closure of the 
establishment, 
the wages payable to him shall be paid within two working days of his removal, dismissal, retrenchment 
or, as the case may be, his resignation. 
(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub -section ( 1) or sub -section ( 2), the appropriate 
Government may, provide any other time limit for payment of wages where it considers reasonable 
having regard to the circumstances under which the wages are to be paid. 
(4) Nothing contained in sub -section (1) or sub-section (2) shall affect any time limit for payment of 
wages provided in any other law for the time being in force.

COW2019:s39.heading: Time limit for payment of bonus
COW2019:s39.text:
39 .Time limit for payment of bonus .—(1) All amounts payable to an employee by way of bonus 
under this Code shall be paid by crediting it in the bank account of the employee by his employer within a 
period of eight months from the close of the accounting year: 
Provided that the appropriate Government or such authority as the appropriate Government may 
specify in this behalf may, upon an application made to it by the employer and for sufficient reasons, by 
order, extend the said period of eight months to such further period or periods as it thinks fit; so, however, 
that the total period so extended shall not in any case exceed two years. 
(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub -section ( 1), where there is a dispute regarding 
payment of bonus pending before any authority, such bonus shall be paid, within a period of one month 
from the date on which the award becomes enforceable or the settlement comes into operation, in respect 
of such dispute: 
Provided that if, there is a dispute for payment at the higher rate, the employer shall pay eight and 
one-third per cent. of the wages earned by the employee as per the provisions of this Code within a period 
of eight months from the close of the accounting year.

LSAA1987:s13.heading: Entitlement of legal services
LSAA1987:s13.text:
13. Entitlement of legal services .—(1) Persons who satisfy all or any of the criteria specified in 
section 12 shall be entitled to receive legal services provided that the concerned Authority is satisfied that 
such person has a prima facie case to prosecute or to defend. 
(2) An affidavit made by a person as to his income may be regarded as sufficient for making him 
eligible to the entitlement of legal services under this Act unless the concerned Authority has reason to 
disbelieve such affidavit. 
CHAPTER V 
FINANCE, ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT

COW2019:s14.heading: Wages for overtime work
COW2019:s14.text:
14. Wages for overtime work.—Where an employee whose minimum rate of wages has been fixed 
under this Code by the hour, by the day or by such a longer wage -period as may be prescribed, works on 
any day in excess of the number of hours constituting a normal working day, the employer shall pay him 
for every hour or for part of an hour so worked in excess, at the overtime rate which shall not be less than 
twice the normal rate of wages. 
CHAPTER III 
PAYMENT OF WAGES
COW2019:s14.full_text:

for every hour or for part of an hour so worked in excess, at the overtime rate which shall not be less than 
twice the normal rate of wages.

COW2019:s45.full_text:
45. Claims under Code and procedure thereof .—(1) The appropriate Government may, by 
notification, appoint one or more authorities, not below the rank of a Gazetted Officer, to hear and 
determine the claims which arises under the provisions of this Code. 
 
(2) The authority appointed under sub -section (1), while deciding the claim under that sub -section, 
may order, having regard to the circumstances under which the claim arises, the payment of compensation 
in addition to the claim determined, which may extend to ten times of the claim determined and 
endeavour shall be made by the authority to decide the claim within a period of three months. 
(3) If an employer fails to pay the claim determined and compensation ordered to be paid under sub -
section (2), the authority shall issue a certificate of recovery to the Collector or District Magistrate of the 
district where the establishment is located who shall recover the same as arrears of land revenue and remit 
the same to the authority for payment to the concerned employee. 
(4) Any application before the authority for claim referred to in sub-section (1) may be filed by,— 
(a) the employee concerned; or 
(b) any Trade Union registered under the Trade Unions Act, 1926 (16 of 1926) of which the 
employee is a member; or 
(c) the Inspector-cum-Facilitator. 
(5) Subject to such rules as may be made, a single application may be filed under this section on 
behalf or in respect of any number of employees employed in an establishment. 
(6) The application under sub-section (4) may be filed within a period of three years from the date on 
which claims referred to in sub-section (1) arises: 
Provided that the authority referred to in sub -section ( 1) may, entertain the application after three 
years on sufficient cause being shown by the applicant for such delay. 
(7) The authority appointed under sub -section (1) and the appellate authority appointed under sub -
section (1) of section 49, shall have all the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 
1908 (5 of 1908), for the purpose of taking evidence and of enforcing the attendance of witnesses and 
compelling the production of documents, and every such authority or appellate authority shall be deemed 
to be a civil court for all the purposes of section 195 and Chapter XXVI of the Code of Criminal 
Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974).

advice.plain_summary: You were let go on 30 September 2026 and the family still owes you ₹18,500 for September wages and overtime. Under the law they should have paid you within two days of your dismissal, so the money is already overdue.

claims.text: Wages must be paid within two working days after dismissal.
claims.quote: the wages payable to him shall be paid within two working days of his removal, dismissal, retrenchment or, as the case may be, his resignation.

claims.text: Overtime work must be paid at least twice the normal rate.
claims.quote: the employer shall pay him for every hour ... at the overtime rate which shall not be less than twice the normal rate of wages.

claims.text: A claim for unpaid wages is time‑barred after three years from when the wages accrued.
claims.quote: Three years. When the wages accrue due.

claims.text: You can file a claim with the wages authority (a Gazetted Officer appointed under the Code) who will decide the claim within three months and can order compensation.
claims.quote: the appropriate Government may, by notification, appoint one or more authorities, not below the rank of a Gazetted Officer, to hear and determine the claims which arises under the provisions of this Code.

claims.text: Write a clear demand message (WhatsApp or email) stating the amount owed, the legal deadline (2 days) already passed, and ask for payment within 3 days.
If no response, contact the free legal aid helpline (DLSA) to get assistance filing a claim with the wages authority or to arrange a Lok Adalat settlement.
Gather all proof – UPI screenshots, any work logs, and the demand message you sent – to attach to any formal application.

lawyer_needed_when: the family refuses to pay even after your written demand and legal aid assistance
the wages authority issues a certificate of recovery but the employer still does not comply
you need to pursue a civil suit for recovery of the amount plus compensation

context.label: domestic / household worker paid by a family

evidence.item: A written note of the work: start date, what work, hours/days, agreed pay
evidence.how_to_get: Write it down today in your own words, with dates. Keep it simple and honest.
evidence.why: Your own record made early is useful if the other side later disputes the facts.

evidence.item: Proof of payments you DID receive (UPI history, bank passbook, cash notes)
evidence.how_to_get: Screenshot UPI history or get the passbook updated. For cash, note dates and amounts.
evidence.why: Shows the pattern of pay and the gap in the months that were not paid.

evidence.item: Messages or calls about the unpaid money
evidence.how_to_get: Screenshot WhatsApp/SMS. Note dates of calls and what was said.
evidence.why: Shows you asked for the money and what the other side replied.

evidence.item: Employer's full name, house address and phone number
evidence.how_to_get: Write down the address exactly as it appears at the building/society.
evidence.why: Any complaint or notice needs to name and reach the person who owes you.

evidence.item: Anyone who saw you working there (watchman, neighbour, other workers)
evidence.how_to_get: Note their names and phone numbers. Do not pressure anyone.
evidence.why: Without written terms, people who saw you work can support your account.

evidence.item: Society / building entry records or ID card, if any
evidence.how_to_get: Ask the security desk whether visitor or staff registers exist.
evidence.why: Shows you came to work there on particular dates.

pathways.name: Ask in writing (WhatsApp, email or letter)
pathways.risk: They may ignore it, but it creates a dated record you will need later.
pathways.how: State what is owed, from when, and a date by which you expect it. Keep it polite and factual.

pathways.name: Talk to the free legal aid helpline / DLSA first
pathways.time: A call or one visit to the district court complex
pathways.risk: Help depends on your district's capacity; follow up if you do not hear back.
pathways.note: Free legal services are available to listed categories, including "a woman or a child" and "an industrial workman" [LSAA1987:s12]; NALSA also lists income-based eligibility by state [PROC:nalsa_legal_aid].

pathways.name: Settle through a Lok Adalat (via the DLSA)
pathways.time: Depends on when your DLSA holds one
pathways.emotional: Low to moderate: it is a settlement, both sides must agree
pathways.risk: Works only if the other side is willing to settle.

law.quote: arrive at a compromise or settlement between the parties

pathways.name: Claim before the wages authority (labour office)
pathways.time: Months; the law asks the authority to try to decide within three months
pathways.emotional: Moderate: forms, hearings, facing the employer
pathways.risk: Which office handles it depends on your state's rules. For household work, coverage itself may be disputed.

law.quote: endeavour shall be made by the authority to decide the claim within a period of three months

pathways.note: The authority can order compensation that "may extend to ten times of the claim determined" [COW2019:s45]; that is a maximum, not a promise.

pathways.name: Send a legal notice (yourself or through an advocate)
pathways.money: ₹0 if you send it; roughly ₹2,000–₹10,000 through an advocate (Practical estimate, varies by city)
pathways.risk: It may harden the other side. Anything you write can be used later, so stick to facts.

pathways.name: Recover the money through a civil suit (with an advocate)
pathways.money: Court fee (state-specific, not in this corpus) + advocate fees, often ₹10,000+; Practical estimate
pathways.time: Often a year or more; Practical estimate
pathways.risk: Costly relative to small amounts; outcome uncertain.

pathways.name: Do nothing for now
pathways.risk: Time limits keep running. Waiting too long can end your claim.

pathways.name: Hire an advocate for full representation

coverage_notes.quote: employed on wages by an establishment
coverage_notes.text: The Code on Wages defines an employee as a person "employed on wages by an establishment".

coverage_notes.quote: any place where any industry, trade, business, manufacture or occupation is carried on
coverage_notes.text: An "establishment" is "any place where any industry, trade, business, manufacture or occupation is carried on".

Whether a private home counts as an establishment is not settled by this text, and state rules may add to it. Ask the District Legal Services Authority (free) or the local labour office whether your claim can go to the wages authority. Separately, unpaid agreed pay can also be claimed as money owed under an agreement.

limitation.quote: within a period of three years from the date on which claims referred to in sub-section (1) arises
limitation.trigger: the date the unpaid wages fell due
